title: Make an idea feel like Wuff
markdown:
# Make an idea feel like Wuff

This guide is for people designing Wuff Todo features with an agent. You do not need to code or clone the app. Bring an idea, iterate on a prototype and send Tim a clear specification when it feels right.

Have a contributor workspace? Use [Build a feature](/docs/build) for real repository
work, scope approval and review evidence. The prototype path remains available
without a checkout.

Use the early kit download, starter prompt and feature brief template above. Each build links its source base and exact input hashes.

## Start a ChatGPT Work conversation

Paste this instruction with your idea:

> Read https://wuff-todo.vercel.app/docs/agent-context.md. Help me explore a Wuff Todo feature. Ask about the problem, use Wuff’s actual components and design tokens from the linked prototype kit, and show me a working prototype. Iterate with me before preparing a specification. Do not create a Wuff task until I ask you to hand it off.

The guide is public so an agent can read it without signing into your private lists. Examples use synthetic data. Sharing a guide URL never shares your account or tasks.

## What to share with your agent

- This guide and the particular page relevant to your idea.
- Your goal, who benefits, and examples of what feels awkward today.
- Annotated screenshots or sketches you choose to share.
- Feedback on the prototype: what should happen and what should change.

## What the downloads contain

The **prototype kit** is a Vite/React/TypeScript workspace with the actual shared UI, all component source, seven palettes, DM Sans (including italics), Waffles and a sample interaction using the real TaskRow. Your agent runs it in its available build environment; you do not need a local codebase.

The **skill** is a compact reusable instruction with links to the living guide. Use it when your workspace supports custom skills. Otherwise paste its text into your project instructions or conversation. The skill does not grant tools, hosting or account access.

A prototype builder must support React/Vite projects to use the source directly. If it only supports HTML previews, your agent should explain the limitation and identify the result as an approximation. It must not promise actual-component reuse or a published URL it cannot provide.

## From idea to implementation

Explore → prototype → review together → final specification → shared Wuff task → Tim builds → review the result. The task should stand on its own; the conversation is supporting context.

title: What Wuff does today
markdown:
# What Wuff does today

Wuff Todo helps friends and family manage private and shared lists. It also has an optional Work mode for development tasks. Keep everyday lists fast and approachable; richer features should not make every simple task feel like project management.

## Lists and tasks

- Private lists or shared lists with accepted editors; personal sidebar order.
- List descriptions, seven owner-selected colors, sections, archive/restore.
- Tasks with inline names, explicit completion/reopening, shared manual ordering and one level of subtasks. Children have independent completion; deleting a parent also deletes its children.
- Rich notes stored as Markdown, private note images, explicit Save/Cancel and retained drafts when a save fails or remote content changes.
- Optional calendar due dates, including Today/Tomorrow/custom/clear. A date is not a shared due time. Completing a task removes urgency styling; reopening appends it to the active order.
- Personal views: filtering, grouping, sorting, density and collapsed groups. These do not change someone else’s view or shared manual order. Dragging is unavailable under computed sorting.
- Optional Work lists: Todo, In progress, In review, Blocked, Done; priority, one assignee, external references, stable task links and WUFF keys.

## Permissions are part of the design

| Action                                      | Owner                      | Accepted editor | Non-member     |
| ------------------------------------------- | -------------------------- | --------------- | -------------- |
| Read tasks and notes                        | Yes                        | Yes             | No             |
| Add/edit/complete/delete/reorder tasks      | Yes                        | Yes             | No             |
| Rename/delete/archive list                  | Yes                        | No              | No             |
| Change shared metadata, colors and sections | Yes                        | No              | No             |
| Invite or remove people                     | Yes                        | No              | No             |
| Move a task to an existing section          | Yes                        | Yes             | No             |
| Change own view and reminder preferences    | Yes                        | Yes             | No             |
| Leave the shared list                       | Ownership must be resolved | Yes             | Not applicable |

Access is invite-only. Existing admitted people accept account-bound invitations before seeing tasks; a URL or email does not grant access. Reader-only membership, ownership transfer and public self-registration are not current features.

## Collaboration and integrations

Open screens refresh after list changes, including changes through MCP. Remote updates must preserve unsaved input and offer recovery from conflicts. Failed or uncertain saves never look confirmed.

GitHub linking and issue synchronization exist for owner-authorized repositories. Personal Cursor connections and agent controls exist, but paid execution has a separate operational gate. Shared-list membership never grants someone else’s credentials or credits.

Personal reminders and Settings are implemented. Scheduling, delivery-provider configuration and installed-device notification delivery are separate capabilities: a saved preference is not evidence that a notification can be delivered. Reminder times and daily inclusion are personal; they are not shared task due times.

## Surfaces and boundaries

The responsive website and MCP tools use the same authorized backend; the MCP App adds an embedded interface. An online-only Tauri client shares React components; installed-platform capabilities still need platform-specific proof. A browser prototype is not a native build or a live MCP-host test.

No offline list cache or queued offline edits. No arbitrary palette colors, dark mode, recurring tasks, multi-level subtasks or new admission model by default. These can be proposed as new scope, with their implications explained rather than presented as already supported.

This is the prototyping baseline, not a restriction on useful ideas. Clearly mark proposed changes to existing rules so Tim can assess them.

## Current interaction language

Saved views are personal to each list. Save view updates the current view; Save as
new view creates a named view. Shared list settings separate List details, People,
Only for me and Manage list. Home completion and task-title navigation are separate.
Date shortcuts and Clear date change a draft; Save date commits it.

title: Wuff’s visual language
markdown:
# Wuff’s visual language

Wuff is calm, compact and warm. Waffles is a small companion, not a corporate mascot. Keep tasks and readable controls in charge. Use the live palette selector on this guide to see the same color derivation used by the product.

## Use the actual tokens

Import `listPalette` and `listThemeVariables` from `@wuff/design`, or render `ListTheme` from the shared UI. The selected list drives the full experience: page, sidebar, surfaces, controls, text and focus. Settings drafts do not silently save or preview a new list color. Auth and contexts with no selected list use Blue.

| Palette | Primary accent | Reference tint |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Blue | #315f9b | #eaf1fb |
| Lavender | #7355a3 | #f1ecf9 |
| Sage | #34705a | #e9f4ee |
| Rose | #a23f66 | #fbeef3 |
| Peach | #a5502c | #fcf0e9 |
| Sand | #826619 | #f8f3e3 |
| Slate | #526779 | #edf1f5 |

The reference tint is a palette entry, not a substitute for derived page or surface values. The ten CSS roles are `--wuff-primary`, `--wuff-primary-hover`, `--wuff-background`, `--wuff-surface`, `--wuff-sidebar`, `--wuff-accent`, `--wuff-foreground`, `--wuff-muted`, `--wuff-border`, and `--wuff-control`. Use their semantic Tailwind names (`bg-background`, `bg-surface`, `text-foreground`, `text-muted-foreground`, `border-input`, `outline-primary`). Subtle separators and interactive control boundaries are deliberately different colors.

Semantic status colors stay recognizable across list palettes: review violet, blocked/danger red, done green. Reuse StatusTag and shared CSS rather than deriving these from the list accent.

## Type, spacing and shape

DM Sans is used for headings, body text and controls, with real italic font files for notes. Code is monospace. Use the bundled fonts and license; do not fetch a different family from a CDN.

Shared buttons use a 44px minimum height, 8px radius, 14px/20px semibold labels and 8px internal gaps. Inputs/selects are 44px high, text-base and rounded-md; textareas grow with content. Status tags are compact, non-interactive text/icon badges. These are actual component defaults, not permission to shrink touch targets.

Favor small, purposeful gaps (4/8/12/16/24px) and quiet borders. Keep the task’s completion, name and actions aligned. Current TaskRow CSS has completion and trailing actions at 44px around flexible content, without a permanent empty drag gutter. Read the source when extending a row; historical screenshots may predate its latest layout.

## Actions and feedback

| Intent                        | Existing treatment                                         |
| ----------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------- |
| Primary/add/save              | Button variant primary; filled list accent, explicit label |
| Secondary/cancel              | default or outline; bordered surface                       |
| Quiet utility                 | ghost; named icon or concise words                         |
| Destructive utility           | danger; quiet red                                          |
| Confirm irreversible deletion | destructive; filled red with explicit consequence          |

A new shadcn component is a proposal until integrated. Do not run shadcn init or replace Wuff’s controls with stock shadcn styling. Wuff does not ship every upstream primitive: for example, it uses a native select and several feature-owned dialogs/disclosures rather than a universal Select/Dialog library.

## Voice

Labels such as Save notes, Cancel, Delete list and Allow connection stay literal. A short friendly dog joke can appear in surrounding guidance: “No tasks to fetch,” or “A little more de-tail.” Avoid stacking jokes and never hide failures, permissions or destructive consequences. Keep user-written titles and notes unchanged.

title: Real components, visible behavior
markdown:
# Real components, visible behavior

These demos import Wuff’s shipped React components. The complete inventory below is generated from exported component declarations in `packages/ui/src`, not from the upstream shadcn catalogue. Exact source and signatures are included in the prototype kit.

Use the component search and jump links to find a component by name or source path. Expand a module for its exact props.

## The primitive layer

| Module                 | Exports and API notes                                                                                              |
| ---------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| @wuff/ui/button        | Button: primary, default, outline, ghost, danger, destructive; default/sm/icon sizes; asChild; native button props |
| @wuff/ui/input         | Input: native input props, invalid/disabled/focus styling                                                          |
| @wuff/ui/textarea      | Textarea: native textarea props and shared styling                                                                 |
| @wuff/ui/native-select | NativeSelect: native select props/options; inset decorative chevron                                                |
| @wuff/ui/input-group   | InputGroup, InputGroupAddon, InputGroupButton, InputGroupText, InputGroupInput, InputGroupTextarea                 |
| @wuff/ui/status-tag    | StatusTag: status todo, in_progress, in_review, blocked or done; a label, not a button                             |

InputGroupAddon supports inline-start/end and block-start/end. InputGroupButton exposes xs/sm/icon-xs/icon-sm; use icon-sm or another 44px target for touch actions. The existence of a compact size is not an accessibility guarantee for a new use.

## Feature components

TaskRow, task metadata, notes/editor, due-date controls, task actions, task groups/detail drawer, ListSettings, Sharing, ListApp, personal views, Work metadata, GitHub/agent controls, reminders, sortable controls, Corgi and ListTheme are included. Some depend on FeatureRuntime, parent callbacks, task/list shapes and live state. Use their declared props; do not treat them as isolated zero-configuration primitives.

The starter demonstrates TaskRow with in-memory changes and an injected runtime. For another screen, supply only the local mock methods needed by that flow. Unsupported actions should explain that they are not simulated; do not silently contact real services.

## Source and reuse

`packages/ui/src/features/runtime.ts` defines FeatureRuntime and RuntimeContext. It separates components from routing, requests, image retrieval and account behavior. `@wuff/contracts` supplies public types; `@wuff/design` supplies palette derivation; `@wuff/client` supplies typed interfaces. No database or server packages are needed in a prototype.

Inspect the generated inventory for import paths and signatures, then read the matching file in the archive for event behavior and other exported types. Props are exact for this snapshot; the source manifest identifies the copied version. A new export or variant requires a kit rebuild.

title: Responsive and accessible by design
markdown:
# Responsive and accessible by design

Design the feature so it is usable on a phone and with a keyboard from the first prototype. Existing components provide useful defaults; each new composition still needs review.

## Viewports and content

- Inspect 320px and 390px phone widths, plus desktop around 1280px. Add intermediate widths when the layout changes. Long names, long links and expanded editors must fit without horizontal document scrolling.
- Keep compact task rows readable. Collapse secondary actions where appropriate, with visible labels when expanded. Preserve direct completion and recognizable primary actions. Mobile navigation must remain reachable.
- Let text wrap and containers shrink (`min-width: 0`); avoid fixed widths for main content. Horizontal code/table examples may scroll inside their own labelled region.
- Check both Compact and Comfortable density when changing rows. Test empty, one-item and crowded lists, subtasks, completed tasks, archived/read-only screens and different palettes.

## Input, keyboard and focus

- Target at least 44×44 CSS px for common touch actions. All icon-only controls need accessible names; decorative icons are hidden from assistive technology.
- Use real buttons, labelled inputs, native selects and native disclosure semantics. Placeholder text does not replace a label. Avoid nested interactive controls.
- Keep focus visible. Inline rename supports Enter to save and Escape to cancel; closing an editor or dialog restores focus to the trigger. A modal needs an accessible name, focus management and keyboard dismissal where appropriate.
- Reordering needs a non-drag alternative. Existing sortable controls support keyboard operation and position picking; touch scrolling must remain usable. Sorted/filtered views cannot reorder the shared list incorrectly.
- Explain validation beside its field, use aria-invalid/aria-describedby when needed, announce status without stealing focus, and do not announce every keystroke.

## State and consequences

Show loading, pending/saving, saved, empty, offline/request-failure, denied, stale/conflicting and disabled states where relevant. A failed save retains the draft and provides a clear recovery action. A prototype should distinguish simulated results from actual persistence.

Deletion has explicit confirmation and names affected subtasks/members when relevant. The cancellation path preserves data. Personal preferences must be labelled as personal rather than implying a change for the whole shared list.

## Color, motion and review limits

Text and controls must remain understandable without color. Use semantic text/icons alongside state colors. Aim for WCAG AA contrast (4.5:1 normal text, 3:1 large text and meaningful controls/focus boundaries), checking new combinations against their actual background. Preserve reduced-motion behavior; animation must not be required to understand or operate the feature.

Review keyboard sequence and focus in the rendered prototype, not only its JSX. Browser viewport checks do not prove a physical device, touch keyboard, screen reader or full accessibility conformance. State which checks were performed and leave untested behavior explicit.

Reference: [W3C guidance on text contrast](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/contrast-minimum.html).

title: Prototype without a local codebase
markdown:
# Prototype without a local codebase

Your agent handles the build environment. You review the result through its preview or a shared prototype URL. This guide does not require repository access or live Wuff credentials.

## The technical baseline

Use Vite, React, TypeScript and Tailwind CSS, with Wuff’s actual shadcn-style UI. The downloadable starter has pinned base versions aligned with the app: React 19.3.1, Vite 8.3.5, TypeScript 5.9.x, Tailwind 4.3.x and pnpm 10.33.3, targeting Node 22. Dependency installation needs package-registry access.

The archive contains the complete current shared UI/client/contracts/design source and original package manifests. Workspace packages resolve inside the archive; they are not published npm dependencies. The generated source manifest records hashes for every included file. Preserve the baseline packages when prototyping, and create new compositions under src.

## Agent setup

1. Read the plain-text reference and download the prototype kit from this guide.
2. Extract it into the available cloud workspace. Run pnpm install, then pnpm dev for a preview or pnpm build for a shareable static build.
3. Develop the idea using imports from @wuff/ui and @wuff/design. Do not overwrite them with default shadcn components.
4. Use the available hosting/preview tool when the human requests a shareable prototype. Preserve source/export and an exact prototype version with the URL.

The agent must verify what its environment supports. A skill does not install a compiler, grant a Sites plugin, create an account or publish a website. If the host cannot execute or publish this project, return the source and a supported preview and explain the limitation. Do not claim that this specific starter has been tested inside ChatGPT Work until it has been run there.

## Mock the behavior, keep the rules

Use synthetic sample people, lists, tasks and images. The starter keeps changes in React state; refresh resets them. It uses real TaskRow controls with local callbacks. Account/session behavior, collaboration delivery, image uploads, external integrations and reminder transport need explicit mocks when a proposal exercises them. Unsupported actions visibly explain the limitation.

Show owner/editor roles, permission denial, slow/failed/conflicting saves, long content and empty states as relevant. A successful mock does not prove backend authorization, real notifications or production persistence. New permissions and shared behaviors belong in the final brief as proposed changes.

## Keep the iteration useful

Ask for the goal and demonstrate the main interaction early. Use short choices and annotated images rather than requiring technical decisions from the designer. Keep a decision log so the final brief reflects the agreed design rather than every abandoned idea. Make visual departures deliberate and label any proposed component additions.

For the available cloud/local modes and project context, see [OpenAI’s ChatGPT Work guidance](https://learn.chatgpt.com/docs/use-chatgpt). Availability of a particular builder or plugin must be checked in her own workspace.

title: Send a feature Tim can build
markdown:
# Send a feature Tim can build

When you are happy with the prototype, ask the agent to prepare this brief. A good title names the behavior or user benefit. Put the essential requirements in Wuff notes; link supplementary research and larger documents.

## Feature brief

### Problem and intended users

What is awkward today? Who benefits, and what should become easier?

### Agreed scope

What is included? What stays out of this version? Which parts are existing Wuff behavior and which are new proposals?

### Behavior and states

Describe the main flow, entry points, inputs, outputs and where the user returns. Include relevant empty/loading/pending/saved/error/denied/conflict states and what happens on cancellation or deletion.

### Permissions and personal/shared behavior

Who can see or change this? Is the result personal or shared? Explain any proposed permission change. Include how archived lists and removed access affect the experience when relevant.

### Design reference

Link the reviewed prototype version and its source/export. Check that Tim can open the shared URL in your workspace. Attach annotated phone and desktop screenshots, noting the important interactions. Record the design-kit source commit/hash manifest. Use existing component names and identify new components or token changes as proposals.

### Acceptance criteria

Use observable outcomes: “An editor can save their own daily-list preference without changing the owner’s preference,” rather than “Settings work well.” Include the relevant phone, keyboard/focus and failure-recovery outcomes.

### Open questions and review evidence

List unresolved choices, assumptions, mocked behavior and what was actually checked. Do not turn an unanswered question into a requirement. Keep any later scope change explicit so the prototype and specification remain aligned.

## Save it in Wuff

Ask the agent to create or update the intended task in your shared Work list. It should check for an existing task, preserve prior content, attach only images you approved and verify the result. A task link, prototype link and longer notes link have different jobs: include each with a clear label.

If the agent has no connected Wuff tools or the list is ambiguous, it should provide a ready-to-paste title and notes or ask which list to use. The skill does not grant access. Saving a design brief does not authorize starting a paid coding agent or changing the production app.

Use the existing Work states: Todo for work ready to pick up, In progress while building, In review for feedback, Blocked for an unresolved dependency and Done when agreed acceptance criteria are met. Draft exploration can stay in the design conversation until you choose to save it.

title: Build a real feature
markdown:
# Build a real feature

Use this path when Tim has supplied a contributor workspace connected to the real
Wuff repository. You describe the result and try it; your agent manages code, Git,
verification and the PR. Tim approves technical scope and reviews the result.

For exploration without a repository, use [Make a prototype](/docs/prototyping).
The prototype kit uses mocks and cannot deliver a connected feature on its own.

## Give your agent this starter

> I want to implement a Wuff feature in this repository. Read AGENTS.md and
> docs/contributor-workflow.md, then use the wuff-contributor skill if available.
> Help me define behavior and acceptance criteria, create a codex/ branch and draft
> PR, and request Tim's scope approval before implementation. Handle Git and
> verification for me. Preserve Wuff's components, permissions and recovery
> behavior. Show me a safe preview once the backend is confirmed isolated. Keep
> evidence and remaining gaps in the PR. Do not merge or release. My idea is:

## What happens next

Describe → agree the brief → Tim approves scope → build → try the preview → refine
→ checks and evidence → Tim reviews → Tim merges/releases.

The full contributor workflow follows and is available as a plain-text download.


## Build a Wuff feature safely

This workflow covers real feature work in the repository. The contributor chooses
product behavior and tries the result. Their agent handles Git, code, checks and
the PR. Tim approves technical scope, reviews and merges. A draft PR may be
incomplete; ready for review requires the evidence below.

### Before the first feature

Tim must finish these gates before granting contributor write access:

- Activate and verify main protection with owner review, `check` and
  `Contributor policy`. Current plan and runner billing blocks are recorded in
  [GitHub safeguards](https://github.com/timbenniks/wuff-todo/blob/main/docs/contributor-github.md).
- Give each person their own GitHub credentials and no administration or bypass
  access. Never lend Tim's gh login, production credentials or environment files.
  Prefer upstream read access plus a private fork, where the repository's plan and
  fork settings allow it. They push their feature branch to their fork and open
  a PR to upstream main. Upstream write access also permits changing branch
  workflows and emitting similarly named Actions checks; required owner review
  remains essential. Check names alone are not an adversarial security boundary.
- Supply a disposable workspace with synthetic data. A branch/worktree does not
  isolate commands or secrets. Use a dedicated container/account or hosted
  environment without production credentials, privileged MCP connectors or access
  to Tim's credential files. Repository instructions are not a sandbox.
- Confirm preview database, auth and Blob isolation, restrict preview access and
  disable real notifications, paid agent runs and provider side effects. Do not
  test preview writes until Tim confirms this setup; a Vercel URL proves no data
  isolation.

Repository changes do not provision a contributor sandbox or preview backend.
Until those gates pass, use the mock prototype kit or read-only access.

### 1. Understand and define

Read root/nearby AGENTS.md, implementation plan, product spec, architecture,
development, verification and relevant feature docs. Read the product, design and
accessibility guide. Inspect existing code before inventing another component,
service or dependency.

Create one `codex/` branch and early draft PR using the repository template. Never
reset another person's edits, force push shared work or rebase someone else's
branch. Fetch main and resolve conflicts on the feature branch; ask for technical
help if the correct behavior is unclear.

Fill `## Feature brief` with the problem, intended users, included/excluded
behavior, existing behavior to preserve and testable acceptance checkboxes. Under
`## Scope`, identify files, UI/API interactions and sensitive changes. Resolve
product questions with the contributor in ordinary language. Do not ask them to
choose database designs or approve infrastructure commands.

### 2. Get technical scope approved

Before implementation, obtain Tim's brief and path approval on the PR. Prepare
a mock/proposal while waiting; do not implement outside approved scope. The
contributor cannot authorize sensitive technical changes.

The policy reports a SHA-256 of `## Feature brief` (normalized line endings, HTML
comments removed, outer whitespace trimmed). Tim can compute it read-only from a
trusted checkout:

```sh
gh pr view NUMBER --json body --jq .body > /tmp/wuff-pr-body.md
node --input-type=module -e 'import {readFileSync} from "node:fs"; import {briefHash} from "./scripts/contributor-policy.mjs"; console.log(briefHash(readFileSync("/tmp/wuff-pr-body.md", "utf8")))'
```

Tim posts a comment starting with `/wuff-scope`, followed by JSON on the next line:

```text
/wuff-scope
{"briefSha256":"PASTE_THE_REPORTED_HASH","allowedPaths":["packages/ui/src/features/app/lists/task-row.tsx","tests/task-metadata.test.ts","docs/task-content.md"],"sensitivePaths":[],"allowLargeDiff":false}
```

Paths are exact repository-relative files or `directory/**`. Root wildcards and
path traversal are rejected. Renames require both paths. Sensitive files need
their exact names in `sensitivePaths` as well as an allowed path. Diffs over 800
added/deleted lines require `allowLargeDiff: true` or a smaller PR. The latest
scope comment **created** by Tim's numeric GitHub ID wins; editing it updates that
approval. Revoke by posting:

```text
/wuff-scope
{"revoke":true}
```

Changing the brief invalidates approval. Expanding scope requires renewed Tim
approval. Never impersonate Tim or use his credentials for contributor approvals.

### 3. Implement within Wuff's boundaries

- Reuse components, tokens, typography and interactions from `@wuff/ui`. Preserve
  compact layouts, 44px grouped action targets, keyboard/focus and accessible
  labels. Do not initialize a replacement component system.
- Keep server/domain/database code out of browser bundles. Use existing authorized
  services and preserve API/MCP parity when their shared contract changes.
- Preserve private admission, owner-only list administration, shared editor
  permissions, personal preferences/credentials and online-only behavior. Use no
  real private data in previews.
- Preserve version checks, operation IDs and exact-payload retries. Handle stale
  writes and uncertain saves without duplicate mutations or silently losing drafts.
- Avoid unbounded reads, per-row repeated requests, eager heavy editors and
  duplicate subscriptions. Measure query/request or bundle impact when affected.
- Dependencies, contracts, global CSS/tokens, auth, schema, native permissions,
  CI and deployment changes need Tim's explicit scope approval. Ordinary scope
  approval never authorizes migration execution, provisioning, production deploys,
  paid agent runs or release publication.
- Add meaningful regression coverage for changed permissions, retries, concurrency
  and recovery. Do not weaken tests, hide errors with suppressions, mock away the
  tested behavior or change safeguards just to get a green check.
- Keep one feature per PR, record decisions/evidence in its feature document, and
  report unrelated defects separately instead of expanding scope.

The policy conservatively flags sensitive files. It cannot identify every risky
code path or judge architecture; Tim must inspect semantic changes too.

### 4. Verify and record current evidence

Run `pnpm typecheck`, `pnpm test` and relevant regression checks. For new behavior,
write a meaningful failing regression case before the fix when practical. Use the
configured isolated backend and synthetic accounts for integration tests. Never
fall back to production when local services are unavailable.

For UI changes, exercise 320px, 390px and desktop, long content, keyboard/focus,
labels, relevant palettes and applicable loading/empty/error/denied/conflict
states. Check overflow, cancellation, retries and preserved drafts. Attach
screenshots and reproduction steps. Browser checks do not prove screen-reader or
physical-device behavior; report only accessibility checks actually performed.

For authorized server changes, verify relevant owner/editor/outsider isolation,
revocation, idempotency, concurrent/stale writes and API/MCP parity. Record actual
performance measurements when affected. Native compilation and installed-platform
checks are Tim's local release gate; Vercel's web build is separate evidence.

Fill `## Verification` with commands/results and the full current source commit:

```text
Evidence commit: FULL_40_CHARACTER_HEAD_SHA
```

After new code, rerun affected checks and update evidence; do not just relabel old
results with a new SHA. Under `## Preview`, link the deployment for that commit,
test steps and who confirmed backend isolation. If unavailable, explain the
blocker and local evidence. Never invent a preview or isolation claim.

### 5. Submit for review

Review the entire diff for unintended files, secrets, debug data and regressions.
Match acceptance criteria to observed behavior. Fill `## Remaining work or risks`
with gaps, consequences, rollout steps and responsible people; explain when no
known risks remain. Mark ready only when checks pass and evidence is sufficient.
Policy checks prove scope matching and evidence presence, never truth or quality.

Give the contributor a plain-language summary, PR/preview links and remaining
technical help. Do not merge, push main, deploy or mark the feature released. Tim
reviews UI, architecture, evidence and rollout before merging and can request
changes even when automated checks pass.

### Technical help without blocking the idea

When scope/infrastructure is missing, prepare a concrete handoff: user goal,
proposed technical change, affected files, risks and smallest alternative. Keep
the draft PR/mock reviewable. Never ask a nontechnical contributor to authorize
migrations or production commands.
